title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). X is a curve of type (g,ν) over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, and x is a point of it. Two torsors have already been built.
- P_{X,x} is the set of paths in the fundamental groupoid of the arithmetic moduli stack over Q (the universal-curve level), from a Q̄-rational base point x_0 to the point (X,x). It is a torsor under the arithmetic group M_{g,ν}.
- Q_X = P_{X,x}/π̂ is the corresponding path torsor at the level of M_{g,ν,Q} itself, from {x_0} to {x}. It is a torsor under N_{g,ν} = π_1(M_{g,ν,Q}, x_0).

The structure group sits in an extension 1 → T̂^+_{g,ν} → N_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} → 1. Here T̂^+_{g,ν} is the geometric fundamental group, i.e. the profinite completion of the (orientation-preserving) Teichmüller modular group. Similarly 1 → Ĉ^+_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} → 1.

The NB on this page:
1. Push Q_X forward along the quotient N_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} ('extend the structure group to the quotient'). This gives a Γ_{Q̄/Q}-torsor R_X := Q_X ∧^{N_{g,ν}} Γ_{Q̄/Q} ≅ Q_X/T̂^+_{g,ν}.
2. Functoriality of fundamental groupoids along the structure map M_{g,ν,Q} → Spec Q identifies R_X with a path torsor of Spec Q. The paths run from the geometric point Spec Q̄ (image of x_0) to the geometric point Spec k → Spec Q. The latter has the same fibre functor as Spec Q̃, where Q̃ is the algebraic closure of Q in k.
3. So R_X ≅ Isom(Q̄, Q̃) ≅ Emb(Q̄, k). This is (19).
4. Consequence (20): a trivialisation of R_X is the same as a field isomorphism Q̄ ≅ Q̃, i.e. an embedding Q̄ → k. Such a trivialisation is equivalently a reduction of the structure group of Q_X from N_{g,ν} to the geometric subgroup T̂^+_{g,ν}, or of P_{X,x} from M_{g,ν} to Ĉ^+_{g,ν}.

What it serves: the next page uses this to analyse the 'arithmetic discretification' coming from an embedding φ: K → C. Such a φ reduces the structure groups to the discrete Teichmüller groups. After profinite completion, that reduction only remembers φ restricted to Q̃. Grothendieck then conjectures that the discrete reductions, taken for all X and all (g,ν), recover φ itself. This page is the bookkeeping lemma that pins down exactly what information the profinite reduction carries.
errors: (18) as transcribed reads 'R_X ≅ R_X/T̂^+'; it should read Q_X/T̂^+_{g,ν}. This is a transcription slip, not a mathematical error.

Minor: left/right torsor conventions and the base point for Isom (Q̄ coming from x_0) are left implicit. The identification of the torsor under Spec k with Spec Q̃ uses only that the fibre functor of Spec k → Spec Q depends only on Q̃ ⊂ k. This is correct.

ideas.what: The Galois quotient of the path torsor of the arithmetic moduli stack is canonically the torsor of embeddings Q̄ → k. Splitting the arithmetic structure group down to its geometric part is equivalent to choosing an embedding Q̄ → k.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the étale fundamental groupoid / homotopy exact sequence for M_{g,n} over Q; path torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 fundamental groupoid); standard in anabelian geometry and Galois–Teichmüller theory
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid and the fundamental exact sequence); the Teichmüller tower setting is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Viewing a reduction of the structure group to the discrete Teichmüller group as an 'arithmetic discretification' of the profinite groups π_{X,x}; this page computes the profinite shadow of that reduction.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison between topological and étale fundamental groups under conjugation of embeddings (Aut(C) acting on étale π_1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (comparison theorem, SGA1); questions about conjugate varieties going back to Serre
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the Teichmüller tower and the action of Γ_{Q̄/Q} appear in Esquisse d'un programme

missed.claim: This page shows that the profinite reduction of the structure group determines only the restriction of the embedding to Q̃. Grothendieck (next page) conjectures that the discrete Teichmüller reductions P^φ_{X,x}, over all curves X and all (g,ν), determine an embedding φ: K → C completely. Equivalently: an abstract field embedding should be recoverable from how it discretises the étale fundamental groups of all curves. This page supplies the lower-bound half of that question.
missed.quote: la donnée d'une trivialisation de R_X ... équivaut à la donnée d'un iso (20) Q̄ ≃ Q̃ i.e. plongement Q̄ → k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean formulation of 'is the topology of C recoverable from discrete π_1-structures of curves?' I do not know whether it has been explicitly resolved. It touches questions on wild automorphisms of C acting on Betti versus étale structures. The content on this page itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard torsor-pushforward computation identifying the Galois part of the path torsor with field embeddings. It is correct and routine. The only mildly interesting element is its role in the discretification question formulated on the next page.
transcription_corrections: (18): 'R_X ≃ R_X/T̂^+_{g,ν}' should be 'R_X ≃ Q_X/T̂^+_{g,ν}' (the image has Q_X with the structure group N_{g,ν} as subscript).
Insertion over Γ: reads roughly 'sur son quot. Γ_{Q̄/Q}' or 'sur Γ̂'; the meaning is the quotient N_{g,ν} → Γ_{Q̄/Q}.
(19) subscript: 'Isom_{groupoïde fondamental de Spec Q}(Spec Q̄, Spec Q̃)', rather than 'gr. prof.'.
'P_{X,n}' should be 'P_{X,x}'; the group written Ĉ^+_{g,ν} is probably fraktur T̂^+_{g,ν} (cf. next page).
The second line is 'et ce Γ_{Q̄/Q}-torseur est canonique[ment] ...'.
